description: Send one real email from a connected mailbox or a sender address, to check it can send. From a transactional mailbox (including a send-only service) or a sender address, it is reserved as kind transactional: it also needs the transactional permission and uses that stream's plan, daily cap, suppression list and payment gate. From a campaigns-and-messages mailbox it is kind test, checked against: the suppression list, the mailbox's gap and daily cap, the plan's daily sends. To your own address (one confirmed as a mailbox of this workspace, or a member's sign-in email) that is all: it goes even when the last payment failed or the workspace is restricted. Anyone else gets a real email, so it stops when the payment failed (402 `sendPaymentFailed`) or the workspace is restricted (409 `workspacePosture`), and the workspace sends 10 such tests a day: after that it answers 429 with `details.scope: "testDay"`, `resetAt` and a Retry-After header, and a test to your own address still goes. A suspended workspace, or an account banned from sending, sends no test at all. A test from a transactional mailbox (a send-only service included) is transactional email instead: it needs the `transactional` permission, and it stops while the workspace is restricted or its last payment failed, whoever it goes to. The 10 tests a day and the fresh address check don't apply to it; the transactional stream's own suppression list and daily cap do. A test from a sender address is transactional email too, and it also counts toward the workspace's and the domain's emails a day through Amazon SES. Anyone else's address also needs a fresh check that says it can receive mail, the same gate a new message takes: run check_email_address first. An address on the suppression list, a person who unsubscribed, an address the check found invalid, or one not checked yet or whose check is out of date answers 409 and nothing is sent. One the check couldn't confirm (risky, or it couldn't tell) answers 409 `recipientNeedsReview`: pass `recipientReviewed: true` to send it anyway. Pass your own intentKey so a retry can never send it twice. The answer is the send as reserved: call get_send with its id to see how it went. An owner may limit the API key you call with: to some mailboxes or campaigns, to outreach or transactional email, and to a number of emails a day or in all. Anything outside those limits answers 403 and nothing is sent: `details.scope` names the limit (`keyMailbox`, `keyCampaign`, `keyStream` or `keyTotal`). When the key has sent all its emails for today, it answers 429 with `details.scope: "keyDay"`, `resetAt` and a Retry-After header. A key can't read or change its own limits: ask a workspace owner.

bodyHtml.description: The HTML part. Send bodyHtml, bodyText or both. A cold mailbox adds its signature; a transactional mailbox or a sender address sends the body as given.

bodyText.description: The plain-text part. Send bodyHtml, bodyText or both. A cold mailbox adds its signature; a transactional mailbox or a sender address sends the body as given.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

intentKey.description: Your own name for this one message, up to 255 characters. Send the same intentKey again and you get the same send back, never a second email, with no time limit. Names starting with draft:, warmup: or campaign: are refused.

recipientReviewed.description: true: send even though the address check couldn't confirm the address (risky, or it couldn't tell), because you looked and accept that. It never sends to an address found invalid, one on the suppression list, or one whose check is missing or out of date.
